t: The Great Wall is many walls, not one: the fortifications of rival states from the 7th century BCE, joined in the Qin dynasty and rebuilt by later dynasties, mapped in 2012 at 21,196.18 km of walls and trenches.
The brick and stone walls best known today are Ming work, built after the Ming defeat by the Oirats at the Battle of Tumu, with up to 25,000 watchtowers.
Under the Qing, whose rule extended beyond it, work on the wall for border defence stopped; a 2012 report found that 22% of the Ming wall has disappeared.
dyk: Sticky rice mortar, made of sticky rice soup mixed with slaked lime, was widely used to hold the wall’s bricks together; contrary to urban legend, no human bones or body parts were ever built into it.
ev: The first walls of what became the Great Wall are built
Qin unifies China, and the First Emperor orders new walls to join the fortifications of the northern frontier against the Xiongnu
The traveller Ibn Battuta hears of the wall in Yuan China but finds no one who has seen it
Under general Qi Jiguang, 1,200 watchtowers are built from Shanhaiguan Pass to Changping
The Portuguese Jesuit brother Bento de Góis reaches Jiayu Pass from India, perhaps the first recorded European entry into China through the wall
The Ming general Wu Sangui opens the gates of Shanhai Pass to the Manchus, who go on to consolidate Qing rule over China proper
The Great Wall is voted one of the New 7 Wonders of the World
A survey by the National Cultural Heritage Administration puts the walls and trenches at 21,196.18 km and the Ming wall at 8,850 km

f.made: The states of the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods; the First Emperor of Qin, who joined the northern walls; the Han, the Northern dynasties and the Sui, who repaired and extended them; the Northern Wei, Liao, Jin and Western Xia, who built walls further north; and above all the Ming
f.form: Walls, ramparts, trenches, watchtowers, passes and fortresses of rammed earth, stone and wood and, under the Ming, of brick bound with sticky rice mortar; the sites mapped in 2012 total 21,196.18 km of walls and trenches, the Ming wall 8,850 km
f.where: Across northern China, from Liaodong in the east to Lop Lake in the west; about half of the sites lie in Inner Mongolia and Hebei, and the most visited stretches, among them Badaling, Mutianyu and Jinshanling, near Beijing
f.known: its length along the edge of the Mongolian steppe; the Ming brick walls and watchtowers near Beijing; Shanhai Pass, the “First Pass Under Heaven”; Jiayu Pass at its western end; its election as one of the New 7 Wonders of the World; the myth that it can be seen from the Moon
